summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and microscopic colitis, was readmitted for lethargy, nausea, and weakness one week after a prior discharge. She had recently completed a course of Bactrim for a urinary tract infection and reported worsening fatigue, leg cramps, and loose stools. On admission, she had hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and acute kidney injury, all consistent with adrenal insufficiency. She received IV hydrocortisone and fluids in the emergency department, with rapid improvement in symptoms and normalization of labs. The endocrinology team recommended switching from prednisone to a tapering regimen of hydrocortisone and adjusting fludrocortisone to 0.1 mg twice daily. A chest X-ray revealed a possible osseous abnormality in the thoracic spine, prompting a recommendation for outpatient CT. She remained stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged for endocrinology and imaging.
